newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC says introduces smallest LCD digital camera.
newsitem.headline: NEC says introduces smallest LCD digital camera.

text.p: Electronics giant NEC Corp on Thursday unveiled in Japan what it said was the world"s smallest digital camera with a liquid crystal display (LCD) monitor.
The Pinoca measures weighs just 185 grams (6.53 ounces) and can fit into a shirt pocket, NEC said in a statement.
NEC said it will begin shipping the camera on March 14, and projects sales of 120,000 units in the first year.
The price of a basic model will be 69,800 yen ($562), it added.
The camera is powered by two AA batteries and its pictures can be downloaded into a personal computer for viewing, NEC said.
The company said it was considering selling the camera abroad, but added no decisions had been made.
Digital cameras are growing in popularity, and NEC said it expected the market to reach 800,000 units in the fiscal year to the end of March, five times the size of sales in the previous year.
